purpose: Live, authoritative-source inventory of consumers of the two legacy retirement candidates, corrected after independent review (PR #5631 head 18c7d02ac6bc244494c88427a8dce1a8bfef104d) found the prior version relied only on the derived ai-status.json snapshot and a local git-tag substring search, and incorrectly asserted canonical state carries no PR/head bindings.

reviewer_findings_addressed: P1: canonical task authority must come from rewrite.task_state_store.load_snapshot(refresh_checkpoint=False), not derived ai-status.json; queue/lease projections must come from runtime_state.load_runtime_state/queue_events/queue_event_record; live GitHub PR heads and remote approval refs must be observed through supported APIs (gh api), not inferred from local tag names.
Corrected the false claim that canonical state carries no PR/head bindings: task rows do carry github_review_bridge/delivery_binding when a review is in flight; this task's own row is a live example.

Absence of a historical event is treated as a bounded, source/period-limited observation, not as proof a consumer never existed.

candidate_a.verdict: no current live consumer found at this observation point -- retirement proceeds
candidate_a.verdict_detail: 0 of 42 current V2 task rows (before and after the live GitHub inventory pass, event count stable at 3573) carry a review_decision_intent at all, so none can hit the digest-mismatch branch. 0 of the 202 retained queue intents (200 completed, 2 started, both verified live owner dispatches) carry a frozen review_decision_intent. The migration has 0 real (non-hook) firings in the bounded canonical activity log read (33195 logical events across 515 sources). The one existing regression test that exercised the migration used a synthetic task id absent from all three authorities. This is a live, multi-authority absence at the observation window above, not an inference from local strings or a single derived JSON file; it does not claim the migration was never used prior to this window. Retirement proceeds: the migration function and its call-site branch are removed; a digest mismatch on the lease-recovery path is now uniformly treated as a non-recoverable lease (skip, no mutation), matching the pre-existing test_legacy_collision_fails_closed_when_journal_is_missing_or_mismatched expectation for a missing/mismatched journal, now as the only behavior rather than a fallback.

candidate_b.name: task_brief_only_successor / carry_approval_to_task_brief_only_successor / publish_task_brief_only_successor_proof (github_review_bridge.py) and their carried_task_brief_only branches in task_review_merge_gate.py / auto_integrator.py
candidate_b.description: Let a new commit that only changed the generated .orchestrator/task-briefs/ path inherit a prior commit's already-recorded review approval, publish a git-native carry-forward proof tag, and dispatch the canonical review-gate workflow for that successor head, all without a fresh independent review.

searches_performed.what: Every open, base=dev PR head in both repositories that route through auto_integrator (the only routine consumer lane for this exception), classified with the existing (still-present, pre-retirement) task_brief_only_successor function itself against real GitHub commit data
searches_performed.how: GET repos/{repo}/pulls?state=open&base=dev (paginated) for ajoe734/pantheon and ajoe734/execute-plans, then for each head with exactly one parent, GET repos/{repo}/commits/{head} and run the existing task_brief_only_successor(repository=repo, approved_head_sha=parent, successor_head_sha=head, runner=<cached real commit response>) classifier -- a pure classification call with no publish/carry/gate side effect.
searches_performed.result: 28 open dev PR heads observed (19 ajoe734/pantheon, 9 ajoe734/execute-plans), stable across the full observation window (identical head set before and after the GitHub calls). 0 of the 28 heads classify as a task-brief-only successor under the existing (unretired-at-classification-time) function. Pantheon PR #4837's first commit-files page is full at 100 entries and includes ai-task-archive/index.json plus archive task files -- correctly rejected as a non-brief-only change by the existing paging-bound classifier, not a false 'only touched task-briefs' case. execute-plans PR #569 has 0 changed files and also does not satisfy the classifier's non-empty-change precondition.

searches_performed.what: Exact-match remote review-approval proof refs against the observed open-dev heads and their direct parents
searches_performed.how: git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/{repo}.git 'refs/tags/pantheon-review/approve/*' for both repositories, then intersected the tag suffix (after stripping the ^{} peel marker) against the set of {head, parent} shas from the PR inventory above -- an exact ref-name match, not the local substring regex review-proof|carry (which cannot match this ref shape at all).
searches_performed.result: Remote enumeration returned 1220 ref lines for ajoe734/pantheon and 122 for ajoe734/execute-plans (including annotated-tag and peeled ^{} lines; these are raw ref-line counts, not counts of unique approvals). Exactly one match against the current open-dev head/parent set: ajoe734/pantheon PR #5513, head ab8edbcabe499bcb912c91fc3084706c8ee128a2, tag object 659cfe444d109360bd8c2c132330e3d2e5cac6d1. A follow-up GET of that tag object confirmed: tagger time 2026-09-01T14:28:48Z, tag subject referencing Claude / OPGAP-DISTILL-QUEUE-WAL-SIDECAR-20260901 / PR #5513, message describing a WAL-sidecar fix -- an ordinary original exact-head independent-review approval, not a carry-forward artifact -- and the tagged commit has two non-brief-only changed files. This tag was only read (GET), never created, moved, or deleted, and its existence is not used to infer this PR is mergeable.

candidate_b.verdict: no current live consumer found across every observed open-dev PR head in both repositories -- retirement proceeds
candidate_b.verdict_detail: Every one of the 28 currently open, base=dev PR heads in the two repositories that route through auto_integrator (the exception's only consumer lane) was classified against the real GitHub commit data using the unretired classifier itself, and none qualifies as a task-brief-only successor. The one exact remote approval-proof-ref match found (Pantheon PR #5513) is an ordinary original exact-head approval with a non-brief-only diff, not a carry-forward proof, and was only read. The carry-forward reason/classification has 0 firings in the bounded activity-log read, and no current task's approval/delivery state depends on it. This supersedes the prior version's incorrect claim (drawn only from derived ai-status.json and a local tag-name substring search) that canonical state carries no PR/head bindings and that a review-proof|carry local-tag grep was a sufficient remote check. Retirement proceeds: task_brief_only_successor, carry_approval_to_task_brief_only_successor, and publish_task_brief_only_successor_proof are removed from github_review_bridge.py (along with the TASK_BRIEF_PREFIX / COMMIT_FILES_PAGE_SIZE / MAX_SAFE_SUCCESSOR_FILES constants and _is_task_brief_path helper that existed only to support them); the task_brief_carry_forward parameter and carried_task_brief_only branch are removed from task_review_merge_gate.evaluate_gate/gate_for_task; and the ReviewGate.task_brief_carry_forward classification method, ReviewGate.publish_task_brief_carry_forward publish method, all four call sites, and the now-dead canonical_review_gate_is_green helper are removed from auto_integrator.py. A direct successor that changes only .orchestrator/task-briefs/ paths after an approved head is now rejected exactly like any other unreviewed successor (reason=approval_head_mismatch), not silently approved.
